turns.learner: Hello teacher. I want practise listening, what are they talking about. I think I am good at this.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good to meet you. Here we practise by reading short dialogues in this chat, and finding the main topic.

First, a quick question: when two people talk, how do you decide what they are talking about? Do you look for one word, or more than one?

Tell me in your own words, then try this one.

A: I have a headache and a fever. B: You should see a doctor.

What is the topic: health, travel or sport?

turns.learner: I look one word, the big word. Fever. So topic is health, I am sure.
turns.tutor:
Yes, health is right. Good.

You said you look at one word, "Fever". Sometimes one word is enough, but sometimes one word can be a side detail, not the main subject. So it is useful to check more words too.

Now try a new one by yourself. Tell me the topic, and write which words helped you.

What is the topic: money, weather or food?

turns.learner: Teacher where is the dialogue? I think weather. Maybe the word rain help me.
turns.tutor:
Sorry, I forgot the dialogue. Good question! Here is one of my own examples for the same choice.

A: Lunch is ready! B: Great, I like rice and chicken. A: Come in, it is raining outside.

You said "rain" helped you, so you looked at one word. Please read all the words again.

What is the topic: money, weather or food? Tell me which words help you.

turns.learner: I see rain, raining. Raining is weather word. So weather, yes? Lunch and rice also there but rain is more strong.
turns.tutor:
You are choosing the strongest single word, "rain". A strong word can be true, but it can still be a side detail.

Rule: the topic is what most of the talk is about, not the one word that stands out.

Example, a different one:
A: The train leaves at nine. B: Is the ticket ready? A: Yes, and take a coat, it is cold.

The topic is travel: train, ticket and leaves are about the trip. "Cold" is only a small extra detail.

Now look at the lunch dialogue again. Which words are about the main subject? Try again: money, weather or food?

turns.learner: Ah, lunch, rice, chicken more words. So food? Rain is small extra like cold. I think food, I am sure now.
turns.tutor:
Yes, food is right. You used lunch, rice and chicken, and you saw that rain was only a small extra detail. Well done.

Now try one by yourself, with no help. This is my own example.

A: Is the 6:30 bus late? B: Yes, 20 minutes. A: Sunny today, but I must be at the airport by eight.

What is the topic: health, travel or food? Write the words that helped you.

Tell me the rule in your own words.

turns.learner: Travel. Words help me: sunny, bus, airport. I am sure this one easy.
turns.tutor:
Yes, travel is right. "Bus" and "airport" are good clues, and they both point to the same topic.

One small thing: you also wrote "sunny". That word is only a side detail here. It is not the main subject.

Now please tell me in your own words: how do you choose the topic of a short dialogue? What do you do with the small extra words?

Tell me the rule in your own words.
